edges.effect_quant: The best-supported effects in aging tend to be steady functional gains or slower decline rather than dramatic life extension.
edges.mechanism: Protein intake around 1.2 g/kg/day may influence Sarcopenia through muscle protein synthesis, energy balance, mitochondrial function, insulin signaling, inflammation, or physical reserve. Older populations are heterogeneous, so frailty status, training background, and protein or energy adequacy can strongly shape the observed result.
edges.summary: Protein intake around 1.2 g/kg/day looks protective for Sarcopenia in community-dwelling older adults, with the most credible effects usually being modest improvements in function, body composition, or risk trajectory rather than dramatic rejuvenation. Trials in older adults support some interventions well, while others remain mechanistic or early-stage. This area especially rewards conservative interpretation because hype routinely outruns the data.
edges.caveats: Functional outcomes often matter more than biomarker changes alone. Small short trials can exaggerate benefit, and interventions that help fitter older adults may perform differently in frailer or multimorbid groups.
